consequences: The selected production predicate changes literal fallback Space only for ManagedCommit, including manual suppression. Owned-preedit commits, successful verified edits, Atomic's existing commit, native terminal paths, reducers, owner/epoch/focus revocations, lattice/ranker/DecisionCore/SafetyGate/verifier and model/package/cache reload are retained. No literal phrase enters runtime. Existing glyph append still uses push_tail_char; CommitText additionally updates last_commit_at, as the ManagedCommit path already does. Ordinary positive learning can occur in eventual authorized native checks; no journal deletion or inverse is granted. There is one extra existing CommitText signal in legacy no-apply boundary handling and no timer/wait/retry; performance and client batching effects must be measured rather than inferred. Paired Space release must be consumed without duplicate text. Roll back the scoped source predicate/artifact if native text, latency or delivery regresses; retain original64 and all old failures. Do not install a source-only candidate or relabel the four passing old-byte diagnostics as repair acceptance.
scope_refinement: Only surrounding-capable, nonterminal Legacy managed inputs change. Opaque Legacy fields and terminal purpose retain native Space even when current word mode is ManagedCommit; source tests verify both. No runtime word/phrase predicate exists.
review_refinement: Pass1 requested a real Reset-before-Space-release regression and an explicit migration of ordinary Legacy transport assertions. Preserve all strict predecessor, owner, epoch, revision, delayed receipt, refusal and manual replay assertions. The proposed lifecycle repair retains only already accepted transport press receipts across an immediate same-field committed-boundary Reset, through the existing LayoutGesture owner. It must not preserve any closed-word correction frame or change Disable/FocusOut handling. No new timer, queue or runtime owner. Existing test names are retained for registry continuity. Only the ordinary managed Space handled/CommitText oracle migrates in the named fixture functions; inert provenance, late receipt and rejection assertions remain. Native opaque/terminal helper and coverage are not broadened. The first full run identified three opaque backspace fixtures sharing the literal helper. They retain the native oracle through an explicit caller-declared space_committed=false parameter; the ordinary surrounding fixtures declare true. The test helper does not inspect the runtime predicate to infer its expectation. No production change was required for these three failures.
